This ensures that the subtrees beneath the node are identical in structure, guaranteeing that fusion is well-defined without checking for symmetry at deeper levels [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the evidence ensures subtrees beneath the node are identical in structure, guaranteeing well-defined fusion without checking for symmetry at deeper levels. The source text explicitly states: 'Beneath a marked node, fusion is well-defined if only if all branches contain identical subtrees over the non-coarsened dimensions.' It further explains that this condition allows one to 'rotate the coarsened dimensions to the bottom... where coarsening would be a series of local modifications to the tree,' implying that the structural identity removes the need for complex symmetry checks at deeper levels. Additionally, the text notes that restricting to 'last-level coarsening requests' (where children are leaves) ensures this condition is met, supporting the claim's implication about the guarantee of well-defined fusion.

*   If $b_j(v) = 0$, then $b_j(v') = 0$ (markers are only on split dimensions) [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that if $b_j(v) = 0$, then $b_j(v') = 0$. According to Definition 3.1 in Source [S1], a coarsening operation in dimensions $C$ results in a new splitting label $b(v')$ such that $b_j(v') = b_j(v)$ for all $j$ not in $C$ (i.e., $j ∉ C$). Since the coarsening dimensions $C$ are a subset of the currently split dimensions ($C ⊆ σ(v)$), any dimension $j$ where $b_j(v) = 0$ is by definition not in $σ(v)$, and therefore not in $C$. Consequently, for any $j$ where $b_j(v) = 0$, it holds that $j ∉ C$, and thus $b_j(v') = b_j(v) = 0$. The evidence fully supports the claim.
